"Fuck You" (stylized as "Fuck You!" or "F**k You!"), known as "Forget You" or "FU" for the clean versions, is a song by American singer CeeLo Green.  It was written as a collaboration among Green, Bruno Mars, his production team the Smeezingtons, and Brody Brown. It was released on August 19, 2010, as the lead single from Green's third solo studio album, The Lady Killer (2010). 

"Fuck You" received widespread acclaim from music critics, and was an international commercial success, making the top-10 in thirteen countries, including topping charts in the United Kingdom, and number two on the Billboard Hot 100.

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.wikitext:
In an interview with ''[[NME]]'', CeeLo Green said that, in addition to being about a heartbreak, the song was also about the music industry itself.<ref name="nme-interview-20101006"/>

[[Bruno Mars]] talked about the making of the song during a 2010 interview: "Cee Lo is one of those artists who says whatever it is that he wants to say. And what do you really want to say to a girl who leaves you for a guy with more money? Do you want to say 'good luck? Have fun in life?' No. You want to say, 'fuck you!' And if anyone's going to do it, it's going to be Cee-Lo."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/bruno-mars-talks-his-offer-to-work-with-justin-bieber-20101011/|title=Bruno Mars Talks His Offer To Work With Justin Bieber!|first=Us Weekly|last=Staff|date=November 10, 2010|website=Us Weekly|access-date=January 18, 2024|archive-date=January 18, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240118152922/https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/bruno-mars-talks-his-offer-to-work-with-justin-bieber-20101011/|url-status=live}}</ref>

sections.heading: Versions
sections.wikitext:
Several versions of "Fuck You" have been released, including the original recording, censored copies of it, and newer versions that feature other performers or significant changes to the lyrics.

The original has twice been [[Radio edit#Editing for content|edited to remove swearing]]. The first of these, which is broadcast in the music video on UK television stations and played on US radio, is called "Forget You"; the second, for UK radio use, is entitled "FU".<ref>{{cite news |title=Cee Lo's Viral Hit: Blunt and Sweet |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=129454158 |work=[[All Things Considered]] |date=August 26, 2010 |access-date=August 27, 2010 |archive-date=August 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828060150/http://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=129454158 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Damon |last=Brown |title=Cee Lo's YouTube hit you won't hear on radio |url=http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/30/cee.lo.song.video/index.html |publisher=CNN |date=August 30, 2010 |access-date=August 30, 2010 |archive-date=August 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100830223627/http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/30/cee.lo.song.video/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> These two are essentially identical to the original except in their treatment of profanity; "Forget You" replaces the profanity with sound effects (other than "fuck you", which is changed to "forget you" per the title), and "FU" censors words by simply silencing them except replacing "fuck you" with "eff you", also as its title suggests. The unedited original and both of the censored versions can be found on [[iTunes]], and both "Fuck You" and "Forget You" are included in an extended play featuring the music video and lyric video released on August 19, 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/f-k-you-deluxe-single/390849614 |title=F**k You – Deluxe Single by Cee Lo Green – Download F**k You – Deluxe Single on iTunes |website=iTunes |access-date=October 28, 2011 |archive-date=November 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101130023505/http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/f-k-you-deluxe-single/id390849614 |url-status=live }}</ref> "FU" was not released until September 21.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/fu-single/394582519 |title=FU – Single by Cee Lo Green – Download FU – Single on iTunes |website=[[iTunes]] |access-date=October 28, 2011 |archive-date=May 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513131317/http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/fu-single/id394582519 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A fourth version of the song, featuring American rapper [[50 Cent]], was released to [[iTunes]]. The version was entitled "Fuck You (Heartbreaker)!", and was released only in America. The video for this version of the song incorporates scenes from the original video with extra shots of 50 Cent performing.

CeeLo performed a parody of the song, featuring an [[all-female band|all-female]] [[backing band]] named "[[Scarlet Fever (band)|Scarlet Fever]]", on ''[[The Colbert Report]]'' on November 9, 2010. It is entitled "Fuck You ([[Fox News]])", and satirizes [[Fox News controversies]].<ref name="colbert">{{cite magazine
 |url=http://popwatch.ew.com/2010/11/10/cee-lo-green-colbert-fox-news/
 |title=Cee-Lo Green swaps 'Fox News' for 'F—k You' on 'Colbert'
 |first=Kate
 |last=Ward
 |date=November 10, 2010
 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]
 |quote=Saw you driving 'round town with the girl I love on Fox News / Didn't see one politician that wasn't corrupt on the Fox News, and I get the blues / The poor get poorer, the rich get richer / Ain't that some s— / I'm having pains in my chest because I'm so stressed over Fox News.
 |access-date=February 6, 2011
 |archive-date=February 10, 2011
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210144928/http://popwatch.ew.com/2010/11/10/cee-lo-green-colbert-fox-news/
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref>

A sixth version of the song, entitled "Thank You", was released on May 9, 2011, with lyrics extensively re-written as a tribute to firefighters. These lyrics mention that Cee Lo's mother was a firefighter. A new version of the video was released for this version that includes scenes of Cee Lo visiting a fire station.<ref name="2011May09">{{cite web
 |url=http://www.ceelogreen.com/news,cee-lo-turns-forget-you-into-thank-you_194.htm
 |title=Cee Lo Turns 'Forget You' Into 'Thank You'
 |date=May 9, 2011
|quote=It's a very noble cause, and I connect with it very, very personally because my mother was a fireman as well — one of the first black female firemen in Atlanta, Georgia, so quite a historic accomplishment.

Several versions of "Fuck You" have been released, including the original recording, censored copies of it, and newer versions that feature other performers or significant changes to the lyrics.

The original has twice been edited to remove swearing. The first of these, which is broadcast in the music video on UK television stations and played on US radio, is called "Forget You"; the second, for UK radio use, is entitled "FU". These two are essentially identical to the original except in their treatment of profanity; "Forget You" replaces the profanity with sound effects (other than "fuck you", which is changed to "forget you" per the title), and "FU" censors words by simply silencing them except replacing "fuck you" with "eff you", also as its title suggests. The unedited original and both of the censored versions can be found on iTunes, and both "Fuck You" and "Forget You" are included in an extended play featuring the music video and lyric video released on August 19, 2010. "FU" was not released until September 21.

A fourth version of the song, featuring American rapper 50 Cent, was released to iTunes. The version was entitled "Fuck You (Heartbreaker)!", and was released only in America. The video for this version of the song incorporates scenes from the original video with extra shots of 50 Cent performing.

CeeLo performed a parody of the song, featuring an all-female backing band named "Scarlet Fever", on The Colbert Report on November 9, 2010. It is entitled "Fuck You (Fox News)", and satirizes Fox News controversies.

A sixth version of the song, entitled "Thank You", was released on May 9, 2011, with lyrics extensively re-written as a tribute to firefighters. These lyrics mention that Cee Lo's mother was a firefighter. A new version of the video was released for this version that includes scenes of Cee Lo visiting a fire station.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
Initially, a lyric video for "Fuck You" was released to [[YouTube]] on August 19, 2010,<ref>{{cite web|first=Cee Lo|last=Green|author-link=Cee Lo Green|url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CAV0XrbEwNc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/CAV0XrbEwNc |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Cee Lo Green – FUCK YOU|via=[[YouTube]]|date=August 19, 2010|access-date=August 27, 2010}}{{cbignore}}</ref> featuring [[kinetic typography]], with the lyrics of the song appearing on different colored backgrounds with [[film grain]] overlaid on the video. The same thing was done in the [[German language|German]], [[Japanese language|Japanese]] and [[Spanish language|Spanish]] versions of the video, translating the lyrics, although the vocals remained in [[English language|English]].

The official music video was released on September 1, 2010.<ref name="Green">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pc0mxOXbWIU|title=Cee Lo Green – FUCK YOU (Official Video)|first=Cee Lo|last=Green|author-link=Cee Lo Green|date=September 1, 2010|via=[[YouTube]]|access-date=September 6, 2010|archive-date=October 17, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101017115024/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pc0mxOXbWIU|url-status=live}}</ref> The video was directed by Matt Stawski and was filmed at Cadillac Jack's, a movie prop diner located in the Sun Valley area of [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="Green"/> Taking place in a [[diner]], the video chronicles Cee Lo's misadventures with a girl he has a crush on, known as "The Heartbreaker" throughout the video. In the beginning, a young Cee Lo goes into the diner with his parents and goes up to the Heartbreaker, who is sitting with another boy. He offers to let the Heartbreaker play with his toy [[garbage truck]], but she ignores him and walks away with the other boy, who has a toy [[Ferrari F40]]. In his high school years, Cee Lo works at the diner as a dishwasher. He attempts to woo the Heartbreaker with a bouquet of flowers but slips on fries deliberately dropped by another boy. The flowers fly out of his hand and land on a much younger girl's lap. During his college years, Cee Lo studies in the diner with another woman implied to be his music tutor. He then attempts to woo the Heartbreaker by having the waitress draw a heart-shaped ketchup mark on her hot dog plate, but the Heartbreaker approaches him with a basket of fries and intentionally spills them on his shirt, leaving a large ketchup stain on it and causing the other diner patrons to laugh at him. Humiliated, Cee Lo then goes through an epiphany in his life and the video fast-forwards to the present day, when Cee Lo is now an adult known as "The Lady Killer" and has a fancy [[Cadillac Eldorado]] with his backup singers in the back seat. He drives past the diner to find the Heartbreaker is now working there, sweeping the front entrance while others are dancing behind her. Cee Lo waves at the Heartbreaker before driving away. The final shot is of him waving at the camera and the words "The Lady Killer" appearing on screen, before the shot freezes, thus ending the video.

The [[Radio edit#Editing for content|radio edit]] version of the video contains re-shot elements that have been mixed with parts from the original, most notably when Cee Lo is on screen and he is singing alternative lyrics, but he is not shown singing the ''clean'' lyrics in the titular chorus. Some parts of the video tend to freeze for a split second when a [[Expurgation|bowdlerized]] lyric is being mouthed to prevent the lips from being read. At the start of the explicit version and clean version titled ''FU'', the mother of the young Cee Lo Green can be seen to look very shocked and taps him on the shoulder to make him turn around when he first swears. This does not happen in the clean version titled ''Forget You''.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
In the US, "Fuck You" debuted at No. 69 on [[Hot Digital Songs]] and No. 96 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cee Lo: I Wanted to 'Rock the Boat' with 'F**k You'|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/956526/cee-lo-i-wanted-to-rock-the-boat-with-fk-you|work=Billboard.com|access-date=February 27, 2011|archive-date=October 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007034356/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/956526/cee-lo-i-wanted-to-rock-the-boat-with-fk-you|url-status=live}}</ref> The song originally peaked at number 9 in 2010, but following Cee Lo's performance of the song at the [[53rd Grammy Awards]], "Fuck You" had a resurgence in popularity and climbed back up the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 chart, reaching No. 2 in its 26th chart week (making it one of the slowest climbs ever into the number 2 position) tying it with Cee Lo's previous 2006 hit "[[Crazy (Gnarls Barkley song)|Crazy]]" from his musical duo project [[Gnarls Barkley]] as his highest-charting single. The song remained at No. 2 for four consecutive weeks (kept off the top by [[Lady Gaga]]'s "[[Born This Way (song)|Born This Way]]").<ref>{{cite web|title=Lady Gaga's 'Born This Way' Grows Atop Grammy-Fueled Hot 100|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/472902/lady-gagas-born-this-way-grows-atop-grammy-fueled-hot-100|work=Billboard.com|access-date=February 27, 2011|archive-date=May 2, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502013643/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/472902/lady-gagas-born-this-way-grows-atop-grammy-fueled-hot-100|url-status=live}}</ref> In all, the single spent a total of 48 weeks on the Hot 100. It was certified [[Gold single|Gold]] on November 5, 2010.<ref name="Cee Lo RIAA">{{cite web|title=RIAA Gold & Platinum – Cee Lo|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&title=&artist=cee_lo&perPage=100|publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America]]|access-date=January 28, 2011|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924151606/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the week ending March 20, 2011, the song became the best-selling song of the year so far in the US, having sold 1,865,000 copies, despite never reaching No. 1 and being released in August 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/74345/week-ending-march-20-2011-songs-the-chris-brown-matter/ |title=Week Ending March 20, 2011: Songs: The Chris Brown Matter – Chart Watch |website=New.music.yahoo.com |date=March 23, 2011 |access-date=April 3, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004231137/http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/week-ending-march-20-2011-songs-the-chris-brown-matter.html |archive-date=October 4, 2012 }}</ref> In 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224095314/http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/week-ending-march-27-2011-songs-katy-moves-up.html|archive-date=December 24, 2013}}</ref> The week of April 16, 2011, the song topped the Pop Songs radio airplay chart in its 25th week, completing the longest journey to the summit in the ranking's 18-year history.<ref>{{cite 2012|archive-date=August 7, sections.text:
In the US, "Fuck You" debuted at No. 69 on Hot Digital Songs and No. 96 on the Billboard Hot 100. The song originally peaked at number 9 in 2010, but following Cee Lo's performance of the song at the 53rd Grammy Awards, "Fuck You" had a resurgence in popularity and climbed back up the Billboard Hot 100 chart, reaching No. 2 in its 26th chart week (making it one of the slowest climbs ever into the number 2 position) tying it with Cee Lo's previous 2006 hit "Crazy" from his musical duo project Gnarls Barkley as his highest-charting single. The song remained at No. 2 for four consecutive weeks (kept off the top by Lady Gaga's "Born This Way"). In all, the single spent a total of 48 weeks on the Hot 100. It was certified Gold on November 5, 2010.

In the week ending March 20, 2011, the song became the best-selling song of the year so far in the US, having sold 1,865,000 copies, despite never reaching No. 1 and being released in August 2010. In the subsequent week, the song surpassed 2 million copies in sales in 2011 alone, bringing its total to 3,707,000 copies. The week of April 16, 2011, the song topped the Pop Songs radio airplay chart in its 25th week, completing the longest journey to the summit in the ranking's 18-year history. "Fuck You" would go on to share the record with Demi Lovato's 2012 single "Give Your Heart a Break" before it was eventually broken by Alessia Cara's "Here" in 2016. As of April 2013, "Fuck You" had sold over 6 million copies in the U.S.

sections.heading: Critical response
sections.wikitext: "Fuck You" received critical acclaim. Jason Lipshutz from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' gave "Fuck You" a positive review stating, "it's as sunny as a '60s [[Motown]] hit and as expletive-laden as an early [[Eminem]] song, a combination that fits the singer's sky-high vocals and offbeat sense of humor well. Over a twinkling piano line, bumping bass and steady percussion, Green shakes off a failed relationship with a gold digger by packing the simple pleasures of old-school soul music into tongue-in-cheek verses and a suitably soaring chorus."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Lipshutz|first=Jason|title=Cee Lo Green ,"Fuck You" {{!}} Billboard.com|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/review/1068731/cee-lo-green-fuck-you|date=September 3, 2010|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=October 7, 2010|archive-date=June 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140620013333/http://www.billboard.com/articles/review/1068731/cee-lo-green-fuck-you|url-status=live}}</ref> Nick Levine of [[Digital Spy]] gave the song four out of five stars writing: "As its title suggests, 'Fuck You' is essentially a [[The Finger|middle finger]] extending from the fist of a pop single—and a gloriously catchy Motown stomper of a pop single at that."<ref name="DS">{{cite web|last=Levine|first=Nick|title=Music – Singles Review – Cee Lo Green: 'F**k You' – Digital Spy|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/singlesreviews/a280397/cee-lo-green-fk-you.html|date=October 5, 2010|website=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=October 6, 2010|archive-date=October 7, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007133549/http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/singlesreviews/a280397/cee-lo-green-fk-you.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Alexandra Patsavas, music supervisor for the ''Twilight'' films, praised Mars' ability to veer between "a beautifully crafted pop song exquisitely sung" and the likes of Cee-Lo's "Fuck You". "How sublime that an artist can travel so fluidly between humor and earnestness," she remarked.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/02/08/bruno-mars-grammy-the-smeezingtons_n_1262313.html|title=Bruno Mars Heads Back To Grammys With Production Team, Smeezingtons|author=Ryan Pearson|work=Huffington Post|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=October 17, 2013|archive-date=October 26, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026105149/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/02/08/bruno-mars-grammy-the-smeezingtons_n_1262313.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text: "Fuck You" received critical acclaim. Jason Lipshutz from Billboard gave "Fuck You" a positive review stating, "it's as sunny as a '60s Motown hit and as expletive-laden as an early Eminem song, a combination that fits the singer's sky-high vocals and offbeat sense of humor well. Over a twinkling piano line, bumping bass and steady percussion, Green shakes off a failed relationship with a gold digger by packing the simple pleasures of old-school soul music into tongue-in-cheek verses and a suitably soaring chorus." Nick Levine of Digital Spy gave the song four out of five stars writing: "As its title suggests, 'Fuck You' is essentially a middle finger extending from the fist of a pop single—and a gloriously catchy Motown stomper of a pop single at that." Alexandra Patsavas, music supervisor for the Twilight films, praised Mars' ability to veer between "a beautifully crafted pop song exquisitely sung" and the likes of Cee-Lo's "Fuck You". "How sublime that an artist can travel so fluidly between humor and earnestness," she remarked.

sections.heading: Accolades
sections.wikitext: At the [[53rd Grammy Awards]], "Fuck You" was nominated for [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]] and [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], and won [[Grammy Award for Best Urban/Alternative Performance|Best Urban/Alternative Performance]]. The video was also nominated for [[Grammy Award for Best Short Form Music Video|Best Short Form Music Video]].<ref name="grammy">{{cite web | url = http://www.grammy.com/files/53rdpresslist113010.pdf | title = 53rd Annual Grammy Awards: Final Nominations List | author = National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences | author-link = National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences | date = December 1, 2010 | access-date = December 2, 2010 | archive-date = December 14, 2010 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101214033514/http://www.grammy.com/files/53rdpresslist113010.pdf | url-status = dead }}</ref> It was named the #1 song of 2010 by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'', and made the top of [[Metacritic]]'s users poll.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.13290/title.kanye-west-big-boi-drake-make-time-magazines-top-10-albums/ |title=Kanye West, Big Boi, Drake Make Time Magazine's Top 10 Albums | Get The Latest Hip Hop News, Rap News & Hip Hop Album Sales |website=HipHopDX |date=December 10, 2010 |access-date=January 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002072323/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.13290/title.kanye-west-big-boi-drake-make-time-magazines-top-10-albums/ |archive-date=October 2, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=100064e>{{cite web|url=http://features.metacritic.com/features/2011/users-poll-results-best-of-2010/|title=Best of 2010 Metacritic User Poll Results|website=[[Metacritic]]|date=January 10, 2011|access-date=February 11, 2011|archive-date=March 14, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110314052235/http://features.metacritic.com/features/2011/users-poll-results-best-of-2010/|url-status=dead}}</ref> <!--Spin.com reported that the song was written about Arizona resident Roan Enright.--> ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]'' and ''[[The Village Voice]]''{{'}}s [[Pazz & Jop]] critics' poll named "Fuck You" the best single of 2010. In October 2011, ''[[NME]]'' placed it at number 112 on its list "150 Best Tracks of the Past 15 Years".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/list/150-best-tracks-of-the-past-15-years/248648/page/4 |title=150 Best Tracks Of The Past 15 Years |work=[[NME]] |access-date=October 28, 2011 |archive-date=June 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615155339/https://www.nme.com/list/150-best-tracks-of-the-past-15-years/248648/page/4 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Spin and The Village Voice{{'}}s Pazz & Jop critics' poll named "Fuck You" the best single of 2010. In October 2011, NME placed it at number 112 on its list "150 Best Tracks of the Past 15 Years".

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext:
Cee Lo toured with an all-female backing band named [[Scarlet Fever (band)|Scarlet Fever]], performing "Fuck You" on
''[[Taratata]]'', at the ''[[Reeperbahn]] Festival'', ''[[Later... with Jools Holland]]'', ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'', the 31st annual ''[[Children in Need 2010#Professional performances|Children in Need]]'' telethon, the Christmas edition of [[BBC One]] chart show ''[[Top of the Pops#Christmas specials|Top of the Pops]]'', ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' and [[Scarlet Fever (band)#Live performances|many other venues]]. Cee Lo also performed at the [[53rd Grammy Awards#Performers|53rd Grammy Awards]] on February 13, 2011, with actress [[Gwyneth Paltrow]] and several puppets provided by [[The Jim Henson Company]]. Two days later, he sang at the ''[[2011 BRIT Awards#Performers|2011 BRIT Awards]]'' alongside UK singer [[Paloma Faith]]. On August 14, Cee Lo sang at [[WWE]]'s [[SummerSlam (2011)|2011 Summerslam]] pay-per-view event in [[Los Angeles]] with the addition of [[WWE Diva]]s dancing to "Fuck You" at [[Staples Center|the event's venue]]. During CeeLo Green Presents Loberace, Green performed "Fuck You" with the animatronic band [[The Rock-afire Explosion]]. In 2022, Bruno Mars covered "Fuck You" as part of a medley with during his [[Bruno Mars Live]] (2022-2024) setlist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/culture/music/mars-landing-is-out-of-this-world-20221015-p5bpzk.html|title=Mars landing is out of this world|last=Zuel|first=Bernard|website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=October 14, 2022|accessdate=February 12, 2025}}</ref> In the [[The Voice of Holland season 13|thirteenth season]] of ''[[The Voice of Holland]]'', "Forget You" was covered by Culmore Bell. The live recording is featured on the album ''The Blind Auditions #4 (Seizoen 13)'', which was digitally released on 6 February 2026.
sections.text:
Cee Lo toured with an all-female backing band named Scarlet Fever, performing "Fuck You" on
Taratata, at the Reeperbahn Festival, Later... with Jools Holland, Late Show with David Letterman, the 31st annual Children in Need telethon, the Christmas edition of BBC One chart show Top of the Pops, Saturday Night Live and many other venues. Cee Lo also performed at the 53rd Grammy Awards on February 13, 2011, with actress Gwyneth Paltrow and several puppets provided by The Jim Henson Company. Two days later, he sang at the 2011 BRIT Awards alongside UK singer Paloma Faith. On August 14, Cee Lo sang at WWE's 2011 Summerslam pay-per-view event in Los Angeles with the addition of WWE Divas dancing to "Fuck You" at the event's venue. During CeeLo Green Presents Loberace, Green performed "Fuck You" with the animatronic band The Rock-afire Explosion. In 2022, Bruno Mars covered "Fuck You" as part of a medley with during his Bruno Mars Live (2022-2024) setlist. In the thirteenth season of The Voice of Holland, "Forget You" was covered by Culmore Bell. The live recording is featured on the album The Blind Auditions #4 (Seizoen 13), which was digitally released on 6 February 2026.
